recipes.name: Slow Cooker Pinto Beans
ingredients_raw: 1 pound dried pinto beans, soaked overnight
1 tablespoon dried oregano, or to taste
1 teaspoon ground cumin, or to taste
5 cups chicken broth, or as needed to cover

steps.text: Place beans in a large bowl and cover with water. Allow to soak 8 hours to overnight. Drain.
Place soaked pinto beans in a slow cooker. Add ham, onion, bell pepper, celery, garlic, oregano, lard, cumin, and bay leaves.
Pour in enough chicken broth to cover all ingredients.
Cook on High until beans are very tender, 5 to 6 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Pinto Beans
raw_recipe.description: Slow cooker pinto beans and ham simmer to tender perfection in a savory broth in your crockpot. It’s easy, just pre-soak your beans the night before!

video.description: Slow cooker pinto beans are delicious and easy! In this video, learn how to make a fabulous crockpot recipe that's perfect for a winter night. These slow cooker pinto beans taste amazing! Plus, cooking them low and slow guarantees tender results.
video.name: How to Make Slow Cooker Pinto Beans

review.reviewBody: I used the seasonings in this recipe and thought the flavor was delicious. I did use a ham shank instead of diced ham, and kale instead of bell pepper and added carrots too, since thats what I had on hand. I the veg up in the FP and added the last 2 hrs of 7 hrs in the slow cooker. My son came home to these and hamemade bread and butter..a comfort meal made in heaven...yummm

I made this but like most recipes I modified it based on ingredients I had available. Instead of bell peppers I used about 5 small sweet red and yellow peppers. Instead of celery I used a 16oz can of stewed Italian tomatoes with the liquid. I used just ham, not black forest. Instead of lard I used butter. I had no chicken broth but I did have a package of dried Au Jus that I mixed with 5 cups of water to make my broth. I used all the spices the recipe suggested but I also added salt and pepper, in addition to a small amount of a random spice blend I have that consistes mostly of habanero, sage, thyme and paprika. I did not pre soak the pinto beans, instead I cooked in slow cooker on high for 5 hours and on low for another 3 hours. It came out so delicious. Top it with a little shredded cheese and sour cream with your favorite cracker and you have a the perfect hearty warm me up dish for a cold winter day.

This is a great recipe and as a time saver, I substituted the dry beans with two cans of drained/rinsed pinto beans. I followed the recipe and cooked down the onions, celery and garlic but then added a nice 1/3 cup of red wine and reduced once more before adding chopped bacon (instead of ham) and a diced chorizo sausage. Added 1/2 tbs of Cumin and 1/4 tsp of cayenne. Cook the added meat thoroughly then added a 1/2 cup off beef stock and the beans. Paired this with the excellent cornbread recipe on this app.

Hello! Thank you for a great and tasty recipe. I cooked this last night, as my husband and I really enjoy crockpot pintos. We enjoyed them served over rice, with smothered squash and air fried chicken thighs… Mmmm.. delicious Southern😃 dinner! I cut up a small boneless ham, instead of bacon, like I usually do. The fat on the ham was plenty, so didn’t need lard. May I offer a courtesy tip: due to slow cooking in crockpot, it’s not necessary to soak the beans and they’re perfectly cooked in 5 hours. They were so good, I just ate some for lunch. Be blessed!

I can't eat pork, so I used smoked turkey sausage in place of ham and "plant butter" in place of lard. Those tweaks were made out of necessity. Otherwise, I made as is the first time. It was good, but not fantastic. I now make this with my own tweaks on spices, adding salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Sometimes I make a vegetarian version with mushrooms instead of meat and smoked paprika to make up for the smokiness the meat would normally contribute. When I have time, I roast the garlic and saute the onions ahead of time, which makes it so much better!

Love this! I used jalapeños instead of bell pepper, butter (didn’t have lard), no cumin and one more small onion. I took out about a cup or two of the beans once finished cooking along with two cups of the liquid and blended it. Chopped chicken would have cooked perfectly with this, making this a soup.

Well I liked it after I altered the recipe. It was so unhealthy as described. Did you notice the amount of sodium per serving! Do not follow recipe if you have high blood pressure , etc. Substitute olive oil for the lard and leave out the ham. Still delicious and way more healthy. Add some smoked paprika if you want a more meaty taste without adding meat. Lard? Does anyone really use lard anymore. Want to clog you arteries? Pinto beans and all beans can be so healthy why ruin them with ham and lard!
I made this exactly as the recipe states with the exception of the 5 quarts of chicken stock. I used only 2 quarts and it was plenty of liquid.

I had to punt as I didn’t have some of the ingredients. I omitted the celery and bell pepper as I didn’t have any and used a leftover ham bone in place of the Black Forest. Supplemented the stock with water and added a can of mild green chiles. Used another writers suggestion of boiling the beans for 5 minutes then resting for an hour in the boiled water. Drained and dumped in a slow cooker - done right at the 6 hour mark. Thank you so much!

Easy and delicious bean recipe. I soaked the beans for 8 hours, any longer and they might have been too mushy. I didn't have any lard so I baked some bacon and used the rendered grease. I also used smoked ham hocks instead of processed ham. Then I cooked it all in the slow cooker on high for about 5 hours. The beans are tender and the ham hock adds some meatiness. One of the easiest and tastiest ways to make beans.

Great recipe! Made the beans taste good. I didn't have time for the crockpot when I decided I wanted some beans for dinner so I put them in my Instant pot. I just put the pot on the chili/bean setting and it cooked the unsoaked beans just right.

This is a very good way to cook your pinto beans. For my half recipe of beans, I used a few ham butt slices, grated my onion, used bacon fat, added couple TBS molasses and 2 drops oil from my jar of calabrian chili peppers. I omitted the oregano. They didn't even need salt or pepper, which surprised me as I make my own chicken broth with no salt and de-fat it. I usually bake my beans in a beanpot ; have tried stove top and instant pot, which disappointed, but this crockpot recipe joins baked as top shelf, really enjoyed them. Thank you.
Instead of the green pepper and celery, I add a can of Rotel

These beans were terrible! Way too salty, because of the chicken broth and the ham. I was skeptical about the Oregano; never heard of it being put in beans. The Oregano gave the beans a horrible, strong taste. It's been several hours since eating them, and my throat is still dried out. If I was going to make this recipe again, I would use water instead of the broth, and eliminate the Oregano.
These beans go fast! Easy to follow recipe, slow cooker makes it a breeze!

Loved it! We had a meaty ham hock left over from Christmas and this was a yummy way to use it up. We fixed some corn bread on the side, and it was awesome. It's also a very affordable meal with plenty of food for leftovers.

I love this recipe! It’s easy to follow and to make simple substitutions for what I have on hand. I didn’t have lard nor ham. So I crisped up some applewood smoked bacon in the oven and used that plus the drippings as my lard and ham substitute. Yummy! I also added kosher salt towards to end (about 1 hour remaining) so it could cook through and allow me to adjust for taste.
Overall good flavor. The family enjoyed it and we decided we might add some salt and a little bit of red pepper for the next time. But we all agreed we'd be happy to eat it again
